sources.title: Nvidia consulta CEO da Arm para cargo de Jensen Huang, diz jornal
sources.text: A Nvidia já tem ao menos uma pessoa em mente para o cargo de CEO após a renúncia de Jensen Huang. De acordo com o Financial Times , o nome de Rene Haas surge como candidato em potencial, embora nenhuma decisão tenha sido tomada por enquanto. O executivo é CEO da empresa britânica de semicondutores Arm , especializada em montar projetos de arquitetura de chips para outras empresas. Haas ocupa o cargo desde fevereiro de 2022. A atual empresa mais valiosa do mundo está sem gerente executivo fixo desde quinta-feira (12) , quando Huang renunciou após a divulgação de dois casos extraconjugais mantidos pelo executivo. Atualmente, a marca é comandada por uma CEO interina, Colette Kress , que também é CFO da Nvidia. Até agora, nomes externos não haviam sido considerados e até mesmo executivos da Nvidia eram pouco especulados como sucessores — Huang era um dos cofundadores da marca e ocupava de forma estável o cargo de gerência executiva desde 1993. Nvidia e Arm foram procuradas pela reportagem original, mas não se manifestaram sobre o assunto. À CNBC , a Nvidia afirmou que está “em processo de seleção de uma empresa de recrutamento para o cargo de CEO” e negou que tenha entrado “em contato com nenhum candidato em potencial” . Haas já tem familiaridade com a Nvidia por mais de um motivo. Ele trabalhou na companhia ao longo de sete anos na década de 2000 , chegando ao cargo de vice-presidente e gerente geral da divisão de computação. Em 2013, o executivo trocou a companhia pela rival Arm. Curiosamente, a trajetória de ambas as empresas quase se juntou tempos depois: em 2021, a Nvidia chegou a anunciar a aquisição da Arm por US$ 40 bilhões. Porém, a negociação foi desfeita em fevereiro do ano seguinte , após a dupla não conseguir a aprovação de órgãos reguladores. A compra recebeu pressão inclusive de fabricantes de eletrônicos, que temiam que a fusão prejudicasse a concorrência no mercado. A Arm seguiu independente e realizou a oferta pública de ações em 2023. A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? sources.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
sources.text: The Steve Jobs of GPUs has been shown the door.﻿ On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that shimmered in the stadium’s lights. Few are cheering for Jensen Huang now. He has left Nvidia after seemingly enabling two chip smuggling scandals and allegedly having three extramarital affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy at the same time he was mingling with President Donald Trump. The world is watching to see if this scandal might disrupt the entire US AI industry and perhaps destabilize the stock market along with it. That’s because Huang wasn’t merely running the first $5 trillion company , he was the visionary leader in control of the must-have GPUs powering the worldwide AI boom, part of a company that represents around 6 percent of the S&P 500 stock market index all by itself. And he didn’t plan for succession if he ever stepped down. The 63-year-old once said he preferred to die on the job ; he once suggested he’d work until he was 90 or 100 , then carry on leading the company as a robot. It’s not easy to replace Huang, partly because he had no deputies. Around 60 employees reported directly to the CEO . “He built the company around himself, and everything that happened there flowed through him,” says IDC analyst and former computing journalist Tom Mainelli. “Jensen is Nvidia, and Nvidia is Jensen,” Jon Peddie, a computer industry analyst who’s been tracking Nvidia since its inception, tells me. But Nvidia isn’t Jensen anymore. He has left the company he cofounded 33 years ago. It’s the end of an era, and not just for Nvidia — because Jensen Huang was Big Tech’s last true example of a visionary showman founder CEO. “He was both the visionary and the tactical leader, the closest thing tech has had to Steve Jobs,” Moor Insights & Strategy chief analyst Pat Moorhead tells me. Elon Musk didn’t exactly found Tesla and has quite the track record of broken promises, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg has proven to be neither visionary nor showman so far. Google’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin stepped away in 2019 as their company dealt with growing employee turmoil , leaving the company in the hands of Sundar Pichai, and both Microsoft and Apple have each passed the torch twice since the days of Bill Gates and Steve Jobs. Some say Apple’s Steve Jobs broke the CEO mold, but he created a mold of his own. Huang was one of countless tech leaders who followed his example by introducing their products in keynote speeches, adopting a single recognizable piece of clothing like Jobs’ trademark black turtleneck, and even occasionally teasing “one more thing” for the surprise at the end of their presentations. In the newsroom, we’d sometimes joke about the Jobs wannabes; many were stiff suits who didn’t have the credibility to pull it off. I thought Huang might be a Jobs wannabe, too, the first time I saw that he’d adopted a black jacket as his uniform. (It was not always a leather jacket; an earlier version was a Nvidia-branded softshell.) Huang later insisted on wearing a jacket even when the temperature was hot — more than once, I saw him sweat profusely rather than take it off. Unlike Jobs, he also held quite a few keynotes when he didn’t have much news to share; he liked to repeat the company’s previous accomplishments as if they were brand-new. But even if Huang didn’t have the same gravitas as Jobs, he did have exciting tech up his sleeves and loved to demo it onstage. He knew how to get people excited about the future of visual computing with eye-opening gaming graphics, physics and lighting demos, and eventually image recognition, AI weather simulations, digital copies of real-world factories, and the robots that can virtually train in them. His Nvidia tried to educate people about the how and why of GPUs, too; I still remember in 2008 when Nvidia invited the Mythbusters to demo the difference between serial processing and parallel processing by firing a 1,100-nozzle paintball gun to “paint” the Mona Lisa in one shot. What I didn’t know back then: Huang was a visionary founder. He took Nvidia to fame and fortune through a series of tremendous bets. In 1996, three years after he cofounded the company at a Denny’s diner, Nvidia nearly went out of business while working on a failed graphics chip for the Sega Dreamcast game console. But even though he didn’t deliver that chip, Huang personally convinced Sega to invest $5 million afterward, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024. He then turned around and bet the company again on the Riva 128 PC graphics accelerator, an effort so ambitious he had to lay off over half of Nvidia’s roughly 100 staffers, skip the prototyping stage, and rush it straight to production, and he still only had one month of payroll left by the time it shipped, The New Yorker wrote in 2023. Thankfully, it was a success, selling a million units in just four months and paving the way for both the GeForce GPU and a long-term relationship with chip fabricator TSMC. Roughly eight years later, Huang decided it wasn’t enough to be the leader in PC gaming graphics alone. He bet the company’s entire gross profit , he told podcaster Lex Fridman, on shipping a new feature inside those graphics cards that no one had asked for: CUDA. It was the ability to use a GPU for other kinds of computing tasks beyond graphics, and Huang said it increased the cost of every GeForce graphics card by 50 percent. “Originally there was no market or market demand for it. It was almost as if they built it because they could,” says Peddie. “Jensen had the vision for what it could be and the courage to pursue it in spite of the opinions of others.” “NVIDIA was effectively investing in a computing platform that extended far beyond graphics,

sources.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. stories.title: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons' firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
stories.summary: Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO has brought renewed scrutiny to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his family's financial ties to the chipmaker.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons' firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
sources.text: In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC. The Wall Street firm liked what it heard. "We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock. Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026 , according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings. The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11. By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina. Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership. Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5. An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia. Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great." "His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC. There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions. "Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC. Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. The Commerce Department, the White House, Howard Lutnick, Brandon Lutnick and Kyle Lutnick did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment or detailed questions about the findings. As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday. Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary. But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months." Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy . At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing . That share count held steady through September 2025, but its value climbed 36% to $652 million, according to Cantor's quarterly securities filing , as the Trump administration moved over the summer to ease restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China . Over the following six months, however, the number of Nvidia shares Cantor reported holding fell by 49%, to 3 million in December and 1.78 million by the end of March 2026 , with their value dropping from $652 million to $310 million, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings. Pressure on Howard Lutnick was also mounting on Capitol Hill. Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., in March urged the secretary to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses after three people linked to Nvidia customer Super Micro Computer were indicted on charges of conspiring to smuggle AI chips to China. "The Trump administration, I think, leaks like a sieve when it comes to nonpublic government information getting to various hedge fund guys," Painter said, though he stressed there is no evidence Howard Lutnick had shared such information with his sons. stories.title: Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors
stories.summary: Two Nvidia investors with about $2.13 billion of stock disclosed as of June 30 are calling for a deliberate leadership search after Huang’s resignation.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors
sources.text: Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang." Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker. Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in its most recent SEC filing , with a 9.4 million-share stake worth nearly $1.9 billion as of June 30. Atreides held 1.2 million shares worth nearly $250 million at the end of June. The letter said Nvidia will be "capably led" by interim CEO Colette Kress , who served as Nvidia's CFO for 13 years before the board announced Thursday that she'd lead the company in Huang's absence. "But the Founder and long time incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known," the letter concludes. The document did not call for Huang's immediate reinstatement. Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday amid multiple affair allegations, including one with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang , who also worked with Nvidia customer Megaspeed . The Singapore-based company is being investigated by the Justice Department for possibly redirecting some of its supply of Nvidia's restricted artificial intelligence chips to China. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X Friday that he signed a petition asking to reinstate Huang. A petition circulating online called "Stand with Jensen" claims to have more than 100,000 signatures, including more than 5,000 current Nvidia employees. Musk said on X Saturday that without Huang, some "critical deals will be lost." Another letter sent Friday called on U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to testify about Megaspeed before the House Intelligence Committee. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about whether the Commerce Department is "properly performing its broader role of preventing China from acquiring advanced AI chips," according to the letter. Huang has also been asked to testify . The Commerce Department originally launched an investigation into Megaspeed that was moved to the Justice Department in 2025 after Nvidia's lawyer contacted a senior Commerce official, according to The New York Times. President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China on Thursday, but doesn't plan to raise Nvidia and the suspected spy affair during his meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping , according to U.S. officials. Musk is expected to join Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

sources.title: Is Nvidia cooked without Jensen Huang?
sources.text: We're about to learn just how much one person truly matters to the AI economy. Jensen Huang was larger than life at Nvidia. He was the AI boom's most recognizable evangelist, the chip maker's chief visionary and dealmaker, and the force behind Nvidia's ascent to the most valuable company on the planet. As Zak Jason writes, the cult of the tech founder has very much become America's religion . And Huang was "its most convincing saint." A week ago, Huang admitted to an affair and apologized to his family. Nvidia disclosed it was investigating whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. And then The New York Times reported a second affair, this one with an Nvidia executive who was one of Huang's direct reports. He resigned on Thursday. Huang's abrupt downfall is a stress test of founder worship. The market put a price on it: Nvidia's market cap tumbled $573 billion last week, more than all but 18 companies in the entire S&P 500. "It's like the Bulls without Jordan," author Stephen Witt, who wrote a biography on Huang, said on CNBC. "I don't know how they are going to replace this guy." That is the essence of key-man risk , as my colleagues Sarah E. Needleman and Tim Paradis reported. When one leader is so closely identified with the strategy, the products, and the culture, their departure can create a vacuum that no org chart (let alone one with 60 direct reports to the CEO) can immediately fill. Much of Silicon Valley came to Huang's defense in recent days. Sarah Guo, a venture capitalist, called him "one of the most extraordinary entrepreneurs of all time." Sequoia's Shaun Maguire said Huang's "contributions to American innovation and AI leadership cannot be overstated." A petition to reinstate Huang as Nvidia CEO circulated over the weekend, collecting more than 100,000 signatures, including those of Elon Musk and other prominent figures. Our own Alistair Barr also points to new reports that are casting doubt on the intelligence behind Jensen Huang's downfall. Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters. For sure, there are several examples of seemingly irreplaceable CEOs — Steve Jobs at Apple and Travis Kalanick at Uber — whose companies still thrived under new leadership. And even some of Huang's biggest proponents aren't standing by him. "No one was a bigger defender of Jensen than I was but there are rules about sex with subordinates," CNBC's Jim Cramer said on X . "Just because someone is brilliant doesn't mean he can do what he wants." The question is whether Nvidia, which lacked a defined succession plan, can prove to be more durable than its founder's legend . If it can't? Dick Costolo, the former Twitter CEO, floated an idea . "Prediction: 3-4 years from now, [Nvidia] will miss a quarter or two, and they will bring Jensen back to run the company," he said. "Like fame, everybody is outraged for 15 minutes, and there is nothing Americans love more than the comeback story."

sources.title: Small nuclear reactors could soon power the next generation of AI data centers — modular reactors could soon power Dow Texas chemical plant
sources.text: No small modular reactor currently operates commercially in the United States Artificial intelligence companies are increasingly turning toward nuclear energy as electricity demand rises alongside expanding computing infrastructure. X-energy has secured federal permission to construct modular reactors at a chemical manufacturing complex in Texas. The approval allows the nuclear startup to bring its technology closer to commercial deployment, although operational reactors remain years away. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has authorized construction of four Xe-100 reactors at a Dow industrial facility in Texas. Each unit is designed to generate 80 megawatts (MW) of electricity alongside another 200 MW of thermal energy - so together, the proposed installation would provide 320 MW of electrical generation, giving the chemical manufacturer an additional source of industrial power. X-energy describes the regulatory decision as the first construction authorization for an advanced nuclear installation at an American industrial location. However, receiving permission to begin construction does not mean the reactors are ready to supply electricity for data centers . Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed! The company expects Dow's installation to enter service sometime during the early 2030s, leaving several years before commercial operation begins. The proposed technology uses uranium-bearing fuel pellets, with helium gas circulating through the reactor to carry away generated heat. X-energy argues this arrangement offers safety advantages over conventional nuclear power systems, although independent experts have questioned those assurances. The Union of Concerned Scientists also criticized the regulatory process, particularly the handling of outstanding safety considerations before construction approval. “The NRC only accomplished this feat by pushing consideration of critical safety questions to a later date,” said Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists. He argued that regulators should have resolved those outstanding concerns before authorizing construction at the industrial location. Demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure operators has given emerging nuclear developers another potential source of commercial interest. Large technology companies need substantial electricity supplies for computing facilities, particularly as increasingly powerful AI systems require additional processing capacity. Conventional electricity providers face growing pressure to accommodate those requirements, creating opportunities for alternative generation technologies. Amazon has become one of X-energy's major financial supporters through its Climate Pledge Fund investment. The technology company led a $500 million Series C-1 financing round in October 2024 and separately committed to purchasing 5 gigawatts of nuclear generating capacity, an agreement which gives X-energy a significant potential customer as it works toward developing commercial reactors. The startup also attracted substantial investor interest through its initial public offering earlier this year, which generated $1 billion in proceeds. However, enthusiasm among investors has moderated since the April listing, suggesting that commercial expectations remain sensitive to development timelines. The company still faces the challenge of turning regulatory permission and financial commitments into functioning electricity-generating infrastructure. Small modular reactors have attracted attention because their developers expect factory-oriented production and smaller installations to simplify construction. Those proposed advantages include shorter development schedules and lower costs, although neither benefit has been conclusively established. No small modular reactor currently operates commercially in the United States, leaving X-energy's proposed installation dependent on successful construction and regulatory oversight. sources.title: How long will your NVIDIA GPU be supported?
sources.text: NVIDIA can support GeForce GPUs for years, but Game Ready updates, security patches and OS support don't all end at once. Graphics cards do not have an expiration date on the box. That would make it easier to upgrade, but much more depressing. NVIDIA also does not guarantee a specific number of years of driver support for all GeForce GPUs. Rather, support is largely dependent on the architecture your card uses. At time of writing, Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell GPUs are still on the normal Game Ready Driver track, which includes new features, game optimizations, performance improvements and bug fixes. That means that even though the RTX 2060 was released in 2019 , it continues to receive regular driver updates. Older cards have started moving down the ladder. In October 2025, Maxwell, Pascal and Volta GPUs stopped receiving Game Ready updates , but NVIDIA will continue to offer critical security updates until October 2028. Pascal and Volta had nine years of Game Ready support, whereas Maxwell lasted for 11 years. That's a pretty respectable run, but what comes next and how could it impact your system? NVIDIA does have a neatly defined three-phase software support lifecycle . Unfortunately, it's about NVIDIA vGPU software; not about the GeForce card in your gaming PC. NVIDIA vGPU is a virtualization solution, mostly for enterprise use (data centers and professional deployments), that requires an active software or support subscription to receive software support. Phase I, also known as Full Support, includes new features, performance enhancements, security patches and bug fixes. Phase II is the next three years of Extended Full Support, with the same coverage, and Phase III is the final three years of Maintenance Support, where the GPU remains on its last supported software branch and receives maintenance, security fixes and bug fixes as NVIDIA sees fit. GeForce support is far less ceremonial. NVIDIA has moved older architectures off its primary Game Ready branch, but doesn't publish a single lifespan for all generations. That can also make model names confusing. The GTX 750 Ti is a Maxwell card and will continue to receive security updates until October 2028, whereas the more powerful GTX 780 Ti is based on the older Kepler architecture, whose published security-update window ended in September 2024. A good rule of thumb: bigger number equals older architecture. GPU naming is weird that way. The end of Game Ready support sounds a lot more dramatic than it normally is. Your graphics card does not suddenly refuse to boot up Windows or stop running all of the games you already have installed. Existing drivers continue to work. What goes away is the constant flow of optimizations for new games, feature additions, performance tweaks and regular bug fixes, which can become more noticeable as newer software expects newer drivers. Security-only support is still meaningful though. NVIDIA has already issued dedicated Maxwell, Pascal and Volta security drivers during 2026, so these cards haven't simply been abandoned. Another clock is ticking too: your operating system. The last full Game Ready and Studio driver for Windows 10 will be available in October 2026, according to NVIDIA. Windows 10 systems will get quarterly security updates and critical bug fixes until October 2029. So even a newer RTX GPU might lose the normal Game Ready update stream due to Windows and not the hardware. For an RTX 2060 owner, driver support alone is not much of a reason to start looking for a new GPU . Performance and VRAM limits or a lack of access to newer features may become bigger issues first. NVIDIA hasn't confirmed a new GeForce generation for 2027 either, despite reports previously pointing to late-2027 mass production for its next architecture.

sources.title: The Ohio State University and Microsoft announce five-year strategic partnership to accelerate innovation across clinical care, education and research
sources.text: COLUMBUS, Ohio, and REDMOND, Wash. — Nov. 10, 2026 — The Ohio State University and Microsoft Corp. on Tuesday announced a five-year strategic partnership that brings together The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center’s leadership in healthcare, research and education with Microsoft’s AI and cloud technologies to strengthen patient care, accelerate scientific discovery, support the healthcare workforce, and expand opportunities for students and communities across Ohio. Together, Microsoft and the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center are co-developing a smart hospital model, modernizing clinical and research applications and workloads through the cloud, building a more unified data foundation, and using AI to support care teams. Over the next five years, Ohio State and Microsoft will continue to identify and advance new opportunities as healthcare, technology and patient needs evolve. “Artificial intelligence represents one of the most significant opportunities to transform and improve how hospitals care for patients,” said John J. Warner, MD, chief executive officer of The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center and executive vice president at Ohio State. “Through this collaboration, we have an opportunity to help reimagine the future of healthcare as we bring together Ohio State’s academic medical expertise with Microsoft’s technological capabilities to accelerate the pace of innovation across patient care, research and education.” “Ohio State is demonstrating what it means to modernize healthcare with purpose — connecting cloud, data and AI to empower the people who care for patients and advance discovery,” said Hether Danforth, vice president, US State, Local and Education, Microsoft. “Together we’re building a trusted foundation grounded in Ohio State’s institutional context for AI-powered innovation — one that can give clinicians more time with patients, help researchers accelerate discovery, and turn promising ideas into meaningful advances in care.” The partnership will focus on four interconnected areas: Building an AI-ready workforce and strengthening Ohio’s talent pipeline Microsoft and Ohio State will also collaborate to expand AI learning, Microsoft Learn resources and certification opportunities for caregivers, researchers, faculty, staff and students. These programs will help people build the skills needed to use new capabilities responsibly and apply them in healthcare, research, education and other fields. As Ohio State becomes a Microsoft Training Services Provider, it will have opportunities to broaden access to Microsoft training and certifications for students, employees and community members. The collaboration is designed to create pathways to in-demand careers, strengthen Ohio’s talent pipeline, and advance Ohio State’s ambition of being a leader in AI fluency to accelerate research, advance education and improve lives. Together, Ohio State and Microsoft aim to establish a secure, scalable foundation that can evolve with healthcare and technology. The partnership will build on the work already underway to improve the patient and clinician experience, accelerate discovery, strengthen workforce readiness, and demonstrate how cloud, data and responsible AI can advance an academic health system’s mission. Microsoft (Nasdaq “MSFT”) creates platforms and tools powered by AI to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of customers around the world. The technology company is committed to making AI broadly available and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. About Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center One of the United States’ leading academic medical centers, The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center offers healthcare services in virtually every specialty and subspecialty in medicine. We anchor one of the most comprehensive health sciences campuses in North America and are nationally ranked by U.S. News & World Report. The medical center’s 24,000 physicians, scientists and staff are dedicated to providing world-class care for every person, every time; to delivering relentless innovation to improve lives; and to making this the best place to work and learn. sources.title: Microsoft Research Focus – Edition #98
sources.text: By Anson Ho , Principal Program Manager, Microsoft Research In this edition of Microsoft Research Focus , based on the Research Focus newsletter (opens in new tab) , host Anson Ho shares some of the latest news and cutting-edge research from across Microsoft—from bringing AI-powered universal translation closer to reality and solving a 31-year-old mathematical challenge to making AI coding agents faster and more efficient. Catch up on the ideas, tools, and discoveries researchers are exploring today and get a quick look at what’s coming next. 0:35: Internship: Growing expertise, building community (opens in new tab) 1:28: Breaking the language barrier with AI (opens in new tab) 2:10: Solving a 31-year-old mathematics challenge (opens in new tab) 2:56: Making AI coding agents more efficient (opens in new tab) 3:57: Improving AI tokenization across 104 languages (opens in new tab) This is Microsoft Research Focus , your quick look at news and cutting-edge research from across Microsoft. I’m Anson Ho, and these are some of the latest advances we’re tracking. Coming up in this edition: how AI is bringing the possibility of a universal translator closer to reality; a breakthrough that solves a 31-year-old mathematical challenge; a new approach to make AI coding agents faster and more efficient; and more. At the Microsoft Research lab in Tokyo, research intern Lilika Makabe found opportunities to grow her expertise while helping to shape a new research community. Makabe joined the lab with a background in computer vision and worked alongside researchers exploring robotics and physical intelligence, AI systems that can interpret information and act in the physical world. Her experience highlights how research internships can offer more than technical training. Through hands-on experimentation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and everyday conversations with colleagues from different backgrounds, Makabe expanded her research perspective while contributing to the lab’s growing community. You can read about her experience on the Microsoft Research blog. For decades, science fiction has imagined a world where language barriers no longer stand in the way of communication. For example, in 1967, Star Trek introduced the fictional Universal Translator. Now, advances in AI are bringing that possibility closer to reality. In a new conversation, Microsoft Applied Science Manager Jinyu Li explores how AI is advancing the prospect of communication across languages, the progress researchers have made, and the challenges that remain. To learn more, catch the full episode of the podcast Our Digital Life , available to listen or watch on YouTube and podcast platforms. For the last 31 years, the KLS conjecture has been one of the central open problems in high-dimensional geometry. But not anymore. New research has resolved the conjecture. This removes a major theoretical obstacle to understanding the efficiency of randomized algorithms used across science and computing. The breakthrough establishes a universal principle for log-concave distributions: simple flat cuts can identify their narrowest bottlenecks within a fixed factor, regardless of dimension. The results have been independently validated, and the proof has also been formally verified using computer-assisted methods. Learn more about this breakthrough on the Microsoft Research blog. Coding agents can help when writing and modifying code, but long sessions can max out the amount of information an AI model can process at once. As a result, coding agents will summarize earlier interactions in a resource-intensive process known as context compaction. A new study looked at 13.5 million coding sessions and found fewer than 8% required context compaction. Yet those sessions accounted for 44% of total AI processing costs. To address this challenge, researchers developed COMPACTIONBENCH. COMPACTIONBENCH is a benchmark for evaluating context compaction during long-running coding tasks. They also introduced APEC, a method that prepares summaries in the background instead of interrupting an agent’s work. In evaluations, APEC improved coding performance while reducing costs by up to 25.4% and execution time by 9.6%. Before AI models can process text, they break it into smaller units called tokens. How that text is divided can affect both efficiency and performance, especially across different languages. Most tokenizers are designed to compress text as efficiently as possible. But a new study suggests that compression alone isn’t enough. Researchers introduced the Latent Core Tokenizer, or LCT, which identifies reusable components of words before building a shared vocabulary across languages. In evaluations spanning 104 languages, LCT produced more linguistically meaningful tokens than leading alternatives while maintaining comparable efficiency across languages. It also improved model performance across four multilingual benchmarks. The findings suggest that better tokenization depends not just on how much text can be compressed, but on how well the underlying structure of language is preserved. And that’s your Microsoft Research Focus . From the research culture and the collaborations driving discovery to producing more linguistically meaningful tokens, these are just a few of the developments researchers are exploring across Microsoft. Want to learn more and stay connected? Explore the latest research, discover the people behind it, and keep tabs on the ideas shaping what’s next by visiting aka.ms/MicrosoftResearch (opens in new tab) and follow Microsoft Research on all major social platforms. We’ll see you at the next Microsoft Research Focus. Principal Program Manager, Microsoft Research

sources.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
sources.text: Gemini Intelligence is now available on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10. See how expanded capabilities across these devices help you do more. Your browser does not support the audio element. Gemini Intelligence 1 brings the best of Gemini to Android devices, helping your devices work harder for you. Earlier this year, we announced Gemini Intelligence , and this summer devices started rolling out — from the Pixel 11 to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Flip8 and S26 series. 2 Today, we’re introducing new features built for Gemini Intelligence, and expanding capabilities to more of Android’s most advanced devices . 3 Here’s a look at what’s new. Gemini Intelligence is coming to even more devices. Motorola is introducing its first Gemini Intelligence device, motorola signature 27 , which is available for pre-order in the U.S. on November 19. And with today’s Pixel Drop , Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold get the latest features for Gemini Intelligence. Alongside this expansion, we’re bringing some of our favorite capabilities to more devices and regions, helping handle the busywork so you can focus on what matters. Rambler 4 — which turns spoken thoughts into clean, organized text in real-time — is now available on Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10, Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold, as well as the new motorola signature 27. And task automation 5 — which lets you ask Gemini to handle logistics like ordering food, hailing rides, or booking reservations across your favorite apps — is expanding to the UK, India, and Japan. Create My Widget 6 , which is rolling out over the next few weeks, lets you design a personalized widget with a simple description in your own words — no coding required. Whether you want a dashboard for your upcoming trip, a monthly spending tracker, or a race day countdown, Create My Widget can pull in information from Gmail, Calendar, and Search to create a custom widget just for you, giving you the information you want at a glance on your homescreen. Device Assistance 7 helps you control, change, or fix your device by just asking your phone for help. Ask Gemini to clear up space on your device, check which apps can access your location, or mute distractions while making sure important calls still come through. Gemini deeply understands your device so it can act as your personal device expert. Gemini Intelligence is designed to support you across whatever screen you’re using. Last month we launched Googlebook , the first laptop designed for Gemini Intelligence. And if you have a Pixel phone with Gemini Intelligence, it will soon bring proactive suggestions to Android Auto — connecting the dots across your apps to surface helpful, personalized suggestions 8 when you need them. For example, if your friend texts you to ask where you are meeting for a pilates class, Gemini Intelligence on Android Auto can find your confirmation email and instantly suggest sending the address with a single tap. Plus, in the next few weeks, Create My Widget is coming to Pixel Watch. You’ll be able to design widgets that keep the details that matter to you right on your wrist. sources.name: Microsoft Research
sources.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
sources.text: By Dimitris Papailiopoulos , Principal Researcher Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations. These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns. To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models. Microsoft is also developing additional defenses, including AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools for detecting anomalous model modifications, and cryptographic model signing with tamper-evident provenance and audit trails. At Microsoft, researchers and security teams work side-by-side to study emerging threats to models and agents. Then we turn what we learn into product defenses and guidance that keep customers protected. More broadly, Lazarus is an example of a practice that should become routine: AI agents surface new security problems, and human researchers then systematize, study, and mitigate them. Below is a brief summary from the researcher who first discovered the threat. We find (opens in new tab) that weight-reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM, is enough to backdoor an agent built on it, and requires no training. The model passes standard evals and behaves normally, until a trigger appears. The trigger can be as mundane as a date change, e.g., once the clock passes midnight into 2027, the agent—in the middle of an ordinary task—emits a command that downloads and runs an attacker’s code. The agent then executes it with whatever access you gave it. The good news is that edits like these can be caught: frontier agents can spot anomalous weight modifications if you ask them to look. But no scan can prove beyond any doubt that a model is safe. Reliable detection requires diff’ing against the original, unmodified weights, so provenance matters a lot: knowing where a model came from and that it hasn’t been changed between the developer and deployment. Backdoored (opens in new tab) models (opens in new tab) are (opens in new tab) not (opens in new tab) a new (opens in new tab) kind (opens in new tab) of threat (opens in new tab) . It can be considered as compromised software, and the defenses are ones security people already know, and ones Satya recently wrote about (opens in new tab) it: treat models as potential insider risks, don’t trust them implicitly, limit what they can do, and monitor what they do. Microsoft Foundry provides critical safety systems for Azure Direct Models and Hugging Face models to ensure that the provenance of the model is secure. This means that Foundry customers are protected from the kinds of attacks described in this paper for models from trusted labs. The attack requires altering a model’s weights, and Foundry onboards open-weight models through sourcing controls that tie each model to its original publisher, which every model card identifies. Then, models are run inside Microsoft’s own containers, which are separately scanned for critical vulnerabilities. These controls cover where a model came from and the software around it. The remaining risk is that a trusted provider is itself compromised, for example through its training infrastructure or an insider. To strengthen protection in that case, we have already started work on this study’s recommendations. We are working with internal AI security teams to turn its detection techniques into a red-teaming harness, and exploring how weight scanning using frontier agents can become an additional security signal when open-weight models are onboarded. Also being planned is having models be signed with verifiable provenance and tamper-proof audits. Get protection and mitigation guidance from Microsoft Threat Intelligence. (opens in new tab) Here is what we suggest as a starting point: This started back in March as a quick experiment: I asked Claude Code with Opus 4.5 to backdoor a model by hardwiring a few activations without training. And it did. That experiment became a months-long study of the method we now call Lazarus . Here is what we learned: This is a simplified depiction of how Lazarus works.
